items.info: First switch on a cold-and-dark 777. Powers the standby buses.
items.label: Battery

items.info: Both bus tie switches in AUTO. Lets the electrical system isolate buses on its own if a generator drops out.
items.label: Bus Tie

items.info: Primary and secondary ground power switches if a GPU is connected. Skip if you only have the APU.
items.label: External Power

items.info: Hold the selector to START, release to ON. The APU is a small jet engine in the tail that gives you bleed air for engine start and electricity before the big engines are running.
items.label: APU

items.info: Both APU generator switches. Power them on once the APU AVAIL light comes up.
items.label: APU Generators

items.info: Red on the left wingtip, green on the right, white at the tail. Required from engine start to shutdown.
items.label: NAV Lights

items.info: Lights on the inboard tail illuminating the airline logo. Usually on at night.
items.label: Logo Lights

items.info: Air Data Inertial Reference Unit. Needs about 10 minutes to align at typical latitudes — start it early so you are not waiting later.
items.label: ADIRU

items.info: Automatically applies rudder if you lose an engine on takeoff. Set and forget.
items.label: Thrust Asymm Comp

items.info: Three Primary Flight Computers run the 777 fly-by-wire system. Verify all three switches in AUTO and guarded.
items.label: PFC Switches

items.info: Both engine main generators and both backup generators on. The OFF light stays lit until the engine is running.
items.label: Generator Control

items.info: The DRIVE switches mechanically uncouple a generator from the engine. Guards down — you only pull these for an engine fire or seized generator.
items.label: Drive Disconnects

items.info: All four. Stops cockpit windows fogging up at altitude and helps with bird-strike resilience.
items.label: Window Heat

items.info: Engine and wing anti-ice selectors in AUTO. The system turns ice protection on automatically when icing is detected.
items.label: Anti-Ice

items.info: Floor-path lighting that fires automatically if cabin power is lost. Close the guard once armed.
items.label: Emergency Lights

items.info: Overhead Panel. Don and test both crew oxygen masks — verify flow, communications, and normal/100% selector function. Confirm oxygen pressure is adequate on the quantity indicator.
items.label: Oxygen Masks

items.info: Left, center, and right demand pumps in AUTO. They come on automatically when the system needs extra pressure.
items.label: Hyd Demand Pumps

items.info: C1 and C2 electric primary pumps on. The 777 fly-by-wire needs hydraulic pressure to move the control surfaces.
items.label: Hyd EMPs

items.info: The two air conditioning packs take hot bleed air and turn it into the cool, pressurised air you breathe. AUTO lets the system regulate flow on its own.
items.label: Pack 1+2

items.info: Lets each cabin zone be heated or cooled separately so the front and back are not at wildly different temperatures.
items.label: Trim Air

items.info: Both fans recirculate cabin air through the HEPA filters instead of dumping it overboard, which saves bleed air and fuel.
items.label: Recirc Fans

items.info: L, C, and R isolation valves in AUTO. They open and close automatically to keep the bleed manifold pressurised on one side if the other fails.
items.label: Bleed Isolation

items.info: Sends APU pressurised air into the duct so the engine starters have something to spin them up with.
items.label: APU Bleed

items.info: Both engine bleeds armed. They take over from the APU once the engines are stable.
items.label: Engine Bleeds

items.info: Initial state — opened later for fuel balancing if needed.
items.label: Crossfeed

items.info: Left and right main pumps always on. Center pumps on only if there is fuel in the center tank.
items.label: Fuel Pumps

items.info: Forward and aft outflow valves in AUTO. The system handles cabin pressurisation automatically once a landing altitude is set in the FMC.
items.label: Pressurization

items.info: Walk through the CDU pages in order: confirm aircraft and navdata on IDENT, align the position on POS INIT, build the route on RTE, pick the SID and STAR on DEP/ARR, enter weights and reserves on PERF INIT, set takeoff thrust on THRUST LIM, and read your V-speeds off TAKEOFF REF. Hit EXEC after each page.
items.label: FMC Preflight

items.info: Recorded broadcast of weather, runway in use, and field conditions at the departure airport.
items.label: ATIS

items.info: Departure clearance from ground or clearance delivery before pushback. Tells you the SID, initial altitude and squawk code.
items.label: ATC Clearance

items.info: Cross-check the fuel on the EICAS against the loaded flight plan.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: Stabiliser trim per the FMC TAKEOFF REF page. Should land in the green band on the EICAS.
items.label: Stab Trim

items.info: Both at zero. The takeoff roll can swerve hard if either of these is mis-set.
items.label: Rudder & Aileron Trim

items.info: Local pressure. With QNH set the altimeter reads field elevation while you are on the ground.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: The magenta bars on the PFD that command pitch and roll. You hand-fly the bars and the autopilot follows them too.
items.label: Flight Director

items.info: Both autothrottle switches armed so TO/GA mode engages on the takeoff push.
items.label: Autothrust

items.info: Speed bug at V2 + 10, heading at the runway, altitude at initial cleared level. These are what the autopilot and FD will fly to after takeoff.
items.label: MCP Bugs

items.info: Both armed before takeoff. They engage at the thrust reduction altitude and start flying the FMC route and vertical profile.
items.label: LNAV / VNAV

items.info: Guard above the autopilot disconnect button. Up means it is in the way of an accidental disconnect.
items.label: Autopilot DISC Bar

items.info: The little PFD between the captain and FO seats. Verify it is aligned and reading local QNH.
items.label: Standby Instruments

items.info: Minimums reference, baro reference, ND mode and range. WXR/TFC/TERR off for the gate.
items.label: EFIS

items.info: Rejected Takeoff arming. If you abort the takeoff, autobrake slams on max braking the moment thrust comes back to idle.
items.label: Autobrake

items.info: Both throttles at idle and reverse stowed.
items.label: Throttles

items.info: Match the lever to the actual flap position on the EICAS.
items.label: Flap Lever

items.info: Both levers at cutoff. These are the actual fuel valves — moving them to RUN during start is what lights the engine off.
items.label: Fuel Control

items.info: Center Pedestal. Prevents the aircraft from rolling during prep.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Squawk code from your clearance, mode in STBY for now. You will switch it to TA/RA before takeoff.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Self-test the radar before the gate so you know it works. AUTO afterwards.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Both fire handles seated and not illuminated. Pulling one cuts fuel, hydraulics and electrics from that engine.
items.label: Engine Fire Handles

items.info: Press and hold the fire/overheat test button. Verify all the warning lights illuminate, then release.
items.label: Fire Test

items.info: All passenger and cargo doors. The EICAS doors page should show all clear before you can pressurise.
items.label: Doors

items.info: Per security protocols, once both pilots are seated.
items.label: Flight Deck Door

items.info: Disconnect ground power before pushback if you had it plugged in.
items.label: External Power

items.info: The flashing red anti-collision light on top and bottom of the fuselage. Required before any engine start so the ground crew know the engines are about to spool.
items.label: Beacon

items.info: Seat belt signs on before pushback.
items.label: Seatbelt Sign

items.info: Ground crew confirms the tug is attached and the area behind the aircraft is clear.
items.label: Pushback Clearance

items.info: Released for pushback, set if you are starting at the gate.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Real-world Boeing convention is to start engine 2 (right) first so the captain can monitor cross-cockpit. Pull the start selector to START.
items.label: Engine 2 Start

items.info: Move the fuel control lever to RUN once N2 stabilises around 25%. That introduces fuel and the engine lights off.
items.label: Engine 2 Fuel

items.info: Watch for a clean light-off — exhaust temperature, fan speed, fuel flow all rising normally with no hung start or hot start.
items.label: Engine 2 Monitor

items.info: Same sequence: pull the start selector, then fuel control to RUN at ~25% N2. Wait for engine 2 to stabilise before kicking off engine 1.
items.label: Engine 1

items.info: Both engines stable at idle and no caution messages.
items.label: EICAS

items.info: Verify both engine generators are online — no OFF light on either of them.
items.label: Generators

items.info: Hand the electrical load over from the APU to the engine generators now that both engines are stable.
items.label: APU Generators

items.info: Engines now feed the pneumatic system — APU bleed no longer needed.
items.label: APU Bleed

items.info: Engines now feed the pneumatic system — APU bleed no longer needed.
items.label: APU

items.info: Both start selectors return to NORM automatically once N2 is up, but verify here.
items.label: Start Selectors

items.info: Turn on if you have visible moisture or freezing temperatures during start or taxi.
items.label: Anti-Ice

items.info: Move the yoke and rudder full and free on every axis. Confirms the fly-by-wire and all three hydraulic systems are responding.
items.label: Flight Controls

items.info: Per the FMC TAKEOFF REF page. Typically 5, 15, or 20 on the 777 depending on weight and runway length.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Press CANCEL then RECALL on the EICAS to flush old messages and surface any active ones.
items.label: Recall

items.info: Forward-facing white light on the nose gear so ground crew and other aircraft see you moving.
items.label: Taxi Lights

items.info: Wing-root lights that throw light to the side. Useful at night for spotting taxiway turnoffs.
items.label: Runway Turnoff Lights

items.info: Test brakes and nosewheel steering at low speed. Max around 30 kts on straights, 8 to 10 in turns — the 777 is heavy and the tires get hot fast.
items.label: Brakes

items.info: Cross-check the PFDs during taxi — attitude, heading, altimeters, all in agreement.
items.label: Flight Instruments

items.info: High-intensity flashes on the wingtips and tail. Required when on the runway or in the air.
items.label: Strobes

items.info: Bright forward lights on the wings. On below 10,000 ft and on the runway.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Switches the TCAS to full-resolution mode. With it active, the system can call CLIMB or DESCEND to avoid other traffic.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Onboard radar that paints precipitation. Lets you steer around storm cells.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Cross-check the flap position matches what the FMC TAKEOFF REF page expects.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: The Flight Mode Annunciator across the top of the PFD. Before takeoff you should see TO/GA armed for thrust and roll, and LNAV/VNAV armed below.
items.label: FMA

items.info: Stabilise around 55% N1 first to let both GE90s spool together, then push the throttles forward to TO/GA. The autothrottle takes over and sets full takeoff thrust.
items.label: Throttles

items.info: Smooth rotation at 2 to 3 degrees per second to about 12 to 15 degrees of pitch. The 300ER has a long fuselage, so over-rotating will scrape the tail on the runway.
items.label: Rotate

items.info: Once the vertical speed indicator on the PFD is positive and confirmed climbing.
items.label: Positive Climb

items.info: On the speed bugs in sequence: 20 down to 15, then 5, then 1, then UP. Usually starts at acceleration altitude, around 1,500 ft AGL.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Engage CMD A at pilot discretion, earliest around 200 ft AGL.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: RTO arming auto-disengages on takeoff — set the knob to OFF for cleanup.
items.label: Autobrake

items.info: Turn on if you are climbing through icing — visible moisture below 10°C outside air temperature.
items.label: Anti-Ice

items.info: Confirm all three gear show UP and locked on the EICAS.
items.label: Gear

items.info: Confirm flaps are fully retracted before accelerating to climb speed.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: Verify the cabin is pressurising normally on the EICAS.
items.label: Cabin Pressure

items.info: Off above 10,000 ft.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Pilot call. Usually off in smooth air, on if turbulence is forecast.
items.label: Seatbelt Sign

items.info: Set standard pressure (29.92 inHg or 1013 hPa) at the transition altitude.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Cycle on and off based on the ride and turbulence forecasts.
items.label: Seatbelt Sign

items.info: Distance to T/D shows on the FMC PROG page. Quick rule of thumb: take cruise altitude in thousands of feet, multiply by three, that is roughly your descent distance in nautical miles for a 3 degree path.
items.label: Top Of Descent

items.info: Cross-check fuel against the flight plan every 30 minutes or so on long legs.
items.label: Fuel Quantity

items.info: In steady cruise the Flight Mode Annunciator should show speed mode active, LNAV tracking the route, and VNAV PATH holding altitude.
items.label: FMA

items.info: Pull the destination ATIS roughly 50 NM before top of descent. Tells you the runway in use and weather.
items.label: Arrival ATIS

items.info: Brief the runway, approach type, minimums, missed approach procedure, and taxi expectations.
items.label: Approach Briefing

items.info: On the INIT REF page, jump to APPROACH. Enter VREF, pick the landing flap setting, and update arrival winds.
items.label: FMC Approach

items.info: Tune the ILS for the planned runway, either via the FMC nav radio page or the standby tuner.
items.label: ILS Frequency

items.info: A 2 or 3 setting is typical for a dry runway. Use higher values for short or contaminated runways.
items.label: Autobrake

items.info: Set the decision height for an ILS, or minimum descent altitude for a non-precision approach.
items.label: Minimums

items.info: Engine and wing anti-ice if descending through cloud or icing temperatures.
items.label: Anti-Ice

items.info: If ATC tells you to hold, enter it via the FMC HOLD page so the autopilot flies the racetrack for you.
items.label: Holding

items.info: Set the platform altitude for the final approach fix on the MCP. The lowest you should be before glideslope capture or starting the final descent.
items.label: Approach Altitude

items.info: Verify VNAV PATH starts the descent automatically at top of descent.
items.label: Descent

items.info: Back on passing 10,000 ft for visibility.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Below 10,000 ft you are speed-limited to 250 knots in most airspace, unless ATC waives it.
items.label: Speed

items.info: Below 10,000 ft. Seatbelt sign ON for the approach.
items.label: Seatbelt Sign

items.info: Set local pressure passing the transition level on descent. Now your altimeter reads above ground again instead of pressure altitude.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Final verify the ILS is tuned to the correct runway frequency.
items.label: ILS Frequency

items.info: Sanity check that altimeters are reading close to field elevation as you near the runway.
items.label: Altimeters

items.info: Push LOC to capture the localiser, then APP once established. Both LOC and G/S go green on the FMA when captured.
items.label: Approach Mode

items.info: Pre-set the go-around altitude on the MCP. If you push TO/GA, the autopilot immediately captures the right level-off.
items.label: Missed Approach Alt

items.info: First flap step, taken at UP maneuvering speed.
items.label: Flaps 1

items.info: Plan for Flaps 15 / Gear UP / ~170 KIAS at the final approach fix.
items.label: Flaps 15

items.info: At glideslope intercept, around 8 NM out.
items.label: Flaps 20

items.info: Three green lights confirmed on the EICAS — all gear down and locked.
items.label: Gear

items.info: Flaps 25 or 30 on glideslope. Latest by 1,000 ft AGL — you want a stable approach by then.
items.label: Landing Flaps

items.info: Arms the spoilers to deploy automatically the moment the wheels touch the runway.
items.label: Speed Brake

items.info: Looking for LAND 3 with ROLLOUT and FLARE armed if you are letting it autoland. Otherwise plan to disconnect by minimums.
items.label: FMA

items.info: Pull the throttles back to idle around 30 ft above the runway, even with autothrottle on.
items.label: Throttles

items.info: Slow flare to about 3 to 4 degrees of pitch as you cross 30 ft. Touch down on the main gear first, then lower the nose.
items.label: Flare

items.info: Both engines into reverse — keep it smooth and symmetric. The GE90s have a lot of mass to pull back.
items.label: Reverse Thrust

items.info: Pull reverse out of detent at 60 KIAS. Below that the engines can ingest debris kicked up off the runway.
items.label: Reverse

items.info: Manual braking around 40 KIAS disengages the autobrake and gives you direct control to make your taxiway turnoff.
items.label: Brakes

items.info: After an autoland, disconnect once clear of the runway.
items.label: Autopilot

items.info: Back on for taxi-in.
items.label: Taxi Lights

items.info: Off once clear of the active runway.
items.label: Landing Lights

items.info: Off once clear of the active runway.
items.label: Strobes

items.info: Stowed manually after rollout if you forgot, or to confirm it stowed itself.
items.label: Speed Brake

items.info: Clean up flaps once clear of the runway so ground vehicles do not catch on them.
items.label: Flaps

items.info: STBY on the ground means you are not transmitting position to ATC any more.
items.label: Transponder

items.info: Brought back online so it can take over electrics and bleed at the gate, ready for engine shutdown.
items.label: APU

items.info: Set once parked at the gate so the aircraft does not roll.
items.label: Parking Brake

items.info: Both levers to cutoff. The engines spool down to zero N2 over the next minute or two.
items.label: Fuel Control

items.info: Off once the engines have stopped spinning. Tells ground crew it is safe to approach.
items.label: Beacon

items.info: Off once the engines have spooled down.
items.label: Fuel Pumps

items.info: Electric primary pumps off after engine shutdown — no hydraulic pressure needed at the gate.
items.label: Hyd EMPs

items.info: Off on the ground.
items.label: Weather Radar

items.info: Overhead Panel. Seatbelt sign OFF.
items.label: Seatbelt Sign

items.info: Clears the magenta bars so the next crew can set up fresh.
items.label: Flight Director

items.info: Unlocked once at the gate so the cabin crew and cleaners can get in.
items.label: Cockpit Door

items.info: Saves the alignment data for next flight.
items.label: ADIRU

items.info: Off at the gate. Boarding and unloading uses jetway air conditioning.
items.label: Pack 1+2

items.info: Leave running on external power as needed during the turnaround for galley and cabin power.
items.label: APU

items.info: Connect the GPU before shutting the APU down so the aircraft never goes dark.
items.label: External Power

items.info: Final switch — aircraft fully de-powered.
items.label: Battery

description: A long-range wide-body titan; the 777-300ER flies on the GE90-115B, among the most powerful turbofans ever built. Procedures cover the 777-200ER and 777-300ER.
